title: Mechanics: motion, force and momentum
subtitle: Sample block document for the reader pilot — not an official examination paper.

blocks.text: Speed is how fast an object moves; velocity is speed in a stated direction. An object can travel at a steady speed and still have a changing velocity, because the direction of travel can change.
Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity: a = (v − u) / t. A negative acceleration does not always mean slowing down; it means the acceleration points opposite to the chosen positive direction.
Velocity-time graph for a car accelerating uniformly from rest.

figure.alt: Straight line rising from the origin to 20 metres per second at 8 seconds

items: The gradient of a velocity-time graph is the acceleration.
The area under the graph is the distance travelled.
A horizontal section means constant velocity, not rest.

blocks.label: Question 1
blocks.text: A car accelerates uniformly from rest to 20 m/s in 8.0 s.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Calculate the acceleration of the car.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Calculate the distance travelled in this time.

blocks.text: Momentum is mass multiplied by velocity, p = mv. In a closed system the total momentum before a collision equals the total momentum after it, provided no external force acts.

blocks.label: Question 2
blocks.text: A trolley of mass 2.0 kg moving at 3.0 m/s collides with a stationary trolley of mass 1.0 kg. They move off together.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State the principle of conservation of momentum.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Calculate their common velocity after the collision.

items: Total momentum before = total momentum after
